preamble: Unrounding of the close back rounded vowel [u] to [ɯ]. In Tamil, word-final short /u/ is pronounced unrounded, as [ɯ~ɨ]. The Tolkāppiyam grammar calls it kuṟṟiyalukaram, 'short u', because it counts as half a sound unit against one for a full vowel. The vowel is unrounded in literary Tamil as well, and in spoken Tamil the unrounded vowel also occurs medially after the first syllable in a number of words. A full [u] is kept in words of the form (C)VCu such as karu and puḻu and in nicknames like rāju. Wiktionary writes the final vowel as /ɯ/ even in its phonemic transcriptions (ஒன்று /onrɯ/ 'one').

languageExamples.context: Word-final short /u/ (kuṟṟiyalukaram), except in (C)VCu words such as karu and puḻu

examples.note: Wiktionary gives the formal [ondrɯ]; the spoken forms, with /nr/ assimilated to a geminate nasal, are from Schiffman (1999) as cited on Wikipedia.
